Filter a cohort before running eSVD-DE

Source: R/eSVD_helper.R
filter_cohort.Rd

Applies the cohort-level filters that eSVD_helper runs before eSVD, in this order:

  1. Drop every individual with fewer than min_cells_per_id cells, with a warning naming them.

  2. Check the filtered cohort against min_cells, min_ids, min_ids_per_arm and min_cells_casecontrol; on the first failure, warn and return NA.

Dropping first means every threshold describes the cohort that will actually be analyzed.

Usage

filter_cohort(
  seurat_obj,
  id_var,
  case_control_var,
  min_cells = 20,
  min_cells_casecontrol = 20,
  min_cells_per_id = 3,
  min_ids = 4,
  min_ids_per_arm = 2,
  verbose = 0
)

Arguments

seurat_obj

A Seurat object.

id_var

Column of seurat_obj@meta.data naming each cell's individual.

case_control_var

Column of seurat_obj@meta.data holding the case-control status (two levels).

min_cells

Reject a cohort with this many cells or fewer, after the drop.

min_cells_casecontrol

Reject a cohort in which either arm has this many cells or fewer.

min_cells_per_id

Drop every individual with fewer than this many cells; 0 or at least 3.

min_ids

Reject a cohort with this many individuals or fewer, pooled across arms.

min_ids_per_arm

Reject a cohort in which either arm has fewer than this many individuals. The default 2 is the smallest number for which the Welch degrees of freedom are defined.

verbose

Integer; 0 is silent.

Value

Either NA (the cohort was rejected; see the warning), or a list with dropped_individuals (character vector, possibly empty) and seurat_obj (the object with those individuals' cells removed).

Details

min_cells, min_ids and min_cells_casecontrol reject at <=, and min_cells_per_id and min_ids_per_arm at <, so setting one to 0 disables it. min_cells_per_id is the one exception: a value of 1 or 2 would not disable the drop but weaken it, and a surviving one-cell individual has no within-individual variance, so it must be 0 (off) or at least 3.

The four rejections return the same bare NA, so the warning text is what tells a caller which filter fired; each names its own threshold.

Examples

if(requireNamespace("SeuratObject", quietly = TRUE)){
  set.seed(10)
  sim <- generate_null(cell_per_person = 15, num_genes = 40,
                       num_individuals = 8)
  meta_df <- data.frame(sim$covariates[, c("CC", "Sex", "Age")])
  meta_df$Sex <- factor(meta_df$Sex)
  meta_df$Individual <- sim$metadata_individual
  rownames(meta_df) <- rownames(sim$obs_mat)
  # Seurat rewrites "gene_1" as "gene-1" (with a warning); rename first
  count_mat <- Matrix::t(sim$obs_mat)
  rownames(count_mat) <- gsub("_", "", rownames(count_mat))
  seurat_obj <- SeuratObject::CreateSeuratObject(counts = count_mat,
                                                 meta.data = meta_df)

  # drop two cells from one individual: with min_cells_per_id = 15 that
  # individual is removed, with a warning naming it
  seurat_small <- seurat_obj[, -(1:2)]
  res <- filter_cohort(seurat_obj = seurat_small,
                       id_var = "Individual",
                       case_control_var = "CC",
                       min_cells_per_id = 15)
  res$dropped_individuals
  ncol(res$seurat_obj)
}
#> Warning: dropping 1 individual(s) with fewer than `min_cells_per_id` = 15 cells: indiv_1 (13 cells)
#> [1] 105
